metadata.title: /context Check: Read Your Window Before It Fills
metadata.rebuild_notes: Rebuild consolidates 12-beat scaffolded mess to 7 canonical beats: B00 cold open, B01-B03 body, BVDT verdict, BHTF your-turn, BOUT outro. Dropped NBB00-NBB03 (redundant scaffolder output; NBB02 was off-topic cancer template pollution). Renamed B04->BVDT and B05->BHTF to hit canonical bookend IDs while preserving locked narration.

beats.narration_text: She ran /context mid-session. The bar showed 78% full. The grading tool she was building had used 30%. The other 48% was policy documents, LMS exports, and meeting notes she had pasted earlier to gather context. The build had not started. The window was already crowded. Quality degrades monotonically as the window fills. She had not checked the counter once. This is Liam, in for Bear.

props.segment: /context Check: Read Your Window Before It Fills
props.command: /context — how full is my window right now, and what is filling it?
output: Pasted policy docs, LMS exports, notes: 48%
You have not started the task.

beats.narration_text: The context window is a fixed working surface. When it fills, Claude begins dropping earlier content — including constraints, examples, and instructions stated before the crowding happened. Liu 2025 shows quality degrades monotonically with window length, even with perfect retrieval. The conversation is not progress. Code on disk is progress. Instructions in CLAUDE.md are progress. Chat is disposable infrastructure.

items.label: Fixed surface
items.sub: The window has a hard ceiling; new tokens push old ones out.

items.label: Dropped constraints
items.sub: Earlier rules, examples, and instructions fall off first.

items.label: Liu 2025
items.sub: Quality degrades monotonically with window length.

items.label: Chat is disposable
items.sub: Code on disk and CLAUDE.md are progress. The chat is not.

beats.narration_text: Three tools manage the window. /context: run it before any new task to see what is filling it. /clear: wipes the conversation; safe because durable rules live in CLAUDE.md, not the chat, and code on disk survives. /compact focus on X: summarizes conversation history down to a gist when the history still earns its place — mid-task, when the thread matters but the verbatim does not.

items.label: /context
items.sub: Run it before any new task to see what is filling the window.

items.label: /clear
items.sub: Wipes the conversation. Safe: CLAUDE.md and code on disk survive.

items.label: /compact focus on X
items.sub: Summarizes history to a gist mid-task, when the thread still earns its place.

beats.narration_text: The structural fix for heavy reading is a subagent. Instead of pasting 25 student submissions into the main session, spawn a reader subagent: it reads in its own isolated context window and returns a three-section summary. The main session sees three paragraphs, not 25 submissions. The main session window stays available for the build. Run /context first; subagent when the reading is large.

items.label: Main session
items.sub: Your window stays available for the build.

items.label: Reader subagent
items.sub: Reads the 25 submissions in its own isolated context window.

items.label: Three-section summary
items.sub: Returns key findings, patterns or gaps, items that need your attention.

beats.narration_text: Treat the context window like a kitchen counter. Check what is on it before you start cooking. Clear it between unrelated tasks. Move the heavy prep to a separate workspace — the subagent — when the main surface needs to stay clear. The window is your most limited resource in a Claude Code session. /context is the one command that tells you exactly how much you have left.

artifactLines: The context window is your most limited resource in a Claude Code session.
Run /context before every new task; /clear between unrelated ones; /compact focus on X mid-task.
For heavy reads, spawn a reader subagent — its window fills, yours stays clear.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code and run it on your own next reading task. It spawns a reader subagent that returns a three-section summary — key findings, patterns or gaps, items that need your attention — so the main session window stays free for the build. Watch what happens to your /context bar the next time you would have pasted the source text in yourself.

props.segment: Spawn a reader subagent instead of pasting
props.command: Spawn a subagent to read these documents and return a summary. The subagent's job: read [these files / these submissions], produce a three-section report: (1) key findings, (2) patterns or gaps, (3) items that need my attention. Return only the report — not the source text. I will use the report in this session for the build.

props.title: /context Check: Read Your Window Before It Fills
props.subline: For heavy reads, spawn a subagent.
